rows.citation: NeuroML organisation, GitHub; README contributors include Ankur Sinha, Padraig Gleeson, et al. (2025). Neuro-Klea: Knowledge vaLidated Expert AI assistant for neuroscience. GitHub repository NeuroML/neuroklea.
rows.model_type: AI coding/RAG assistant for NeuroML/LEMS models (not a model-testing framework)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - README and MCP tool source show no mutant generation or fault seeding.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - MCP tool only runs a user-supplied LEMS file via pynml/jLEMS; no stimulation battery.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - no eFEL or feature extraction found in the package file tree.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - no protocol selection of any kind.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - no evaluation design described; the agent's evaluator node only checks whether plan steps are finished.
rows.ai_transformations: partial - LLM agent generates and edits NeuroML code and runs simulations, but does not test whether edits preserve behaviour.
rows.software: Neuro-Klea (agent_pkg, rag_pkg, mcp_pkg) https://github.com/NeuroML/neuroklea ; docs https://neuroklea.org ; GPL-3.0 per GitHub API
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Klea creates and edits NeuroML with AI; NeuroSem would add an independent, multi-protocol behavioural drift test for such edits. The two could complement each other.
rows.verification_method: GitHub REST API repo record (created 2025-08-07, pushed 2026-09-11, GPL-3.0); root, agent_pkg and mcp_pkg Readme.md files; mcp_pkg/neuroml_mcp/tools/neuroml_tools.py and agent_pkg/.../evaluator.py source via gh api; neuroklea.org landing page (WebFetch).

rows.citation: JustasB, GitHub user; the CNS2016 slide filename names Birgiolas (2016). MitralSuite: Objective validation of olfactory bulb mitral cell models with NeuroElectro data using NeuronUnit. GitHub repository JustasB/MitralSuite.
rows.model_type: 8 published multicompartment conductance-based mitral cell models in NEURON (e.g. Bhalla & Bower 1993, Migliore 2014)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - compares published models against experimental data; no seeded faults.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - square current injections at a few test-specific amplitudes (rest, passive, AP, threshold); no ramps or rebound.
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes - six NeuronUnit tests: resting potential, input resistance, time constant, AP width, threshold, amplitude.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - stimuli are fixed per test.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - scores all models against pooled NeuroElectro observations (z-scores); no discovery/held-out split.
rows.software: MitralSuite https://github.com/JustasB/MitralSuite (depends on SciUnit/NeuronUnit, NEURON); MIT per GitHub API
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Validates models against experimental data. NeuroSem instead compares a reference model with its edited version, using calibrated tolerances, seeded mutants and a selected protocol battery.
rows.verification_method: GitHub REST API repo record (created 2016-05-20, MIT); README; repository tree and helpers.py (setupTests test list) plus GetResultsSummary.ipynb via gh api; GitHub web page (WebFetch) for the model list.

rows.citation: lakesare, GitHub user (2021). NetpyneUnit: SciUnit tests for NetPyNE models. GitHub repository lakesare/netpyneunit.
rows.model_type: NetPyNE/NEURON network models (e.g. Potjans-Diesmann cortical microcircuit, small synchronisation network)
rows.controlled_mutations: partial - example compares neuromodulator variants (NMDA antagonist, GABA agonist) against expected synchrony; these are scientific manipulations, not fault mutants.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - network-level simulations; no single-cell current-clamp protocol battery.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - network statistics (synchrony, rescaled-network stats), not single-cell eFEL features.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - none; the README focuses on caching simulation results across tests.
rows.software: NetpyneUnit https://github.com/lakesare/netpyneunit (SciUnit + NetPyNE); MIT per GitHub API
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Closest aspect is the PDCM example checking that network statistics survive rescaling, i.e. a behaviour-preserving transformation. NeuroSem targets single-cell NeuroML models with calibrated tolerances, mutants and protocol selection.
rows.verification_method: GitHub REST API repo record (created 2021-06-04, last push 2022-05-12, MIT); root README; examples/synchronization and examples/pdcm READMEs via raw.githubusercontent.com.

rows.citation: Lehtimäki M, Linne M-L (2014). Usability and functionality of NeuroML description language evaluated using three distinct spiking neuron models. Frontiers in Neuroinformatics, Conference Abstract: Neuroinformatics 2014.
rows.model_type: Phenomenological spiking models (Hindmarsh-Rose, Izhikevich, FitzHugh-Nagumo) in NeuroML v2, converted to NEURON
rows.multiple_stimuli: unclear - the abstract does not describe the stimulation protocols.
rows.electrophysiology_features: unclear - outputs are compared with MATLAB references; no feature-based comparison is described.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - a small usability evaluation on three models.
rows.ai_transformations: no - manual model encoding and tool-based conversion only.
rows.software: none (uses NeuroML v2 tooling, NEURON, MATLAB)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Early evidence that NeuroML-to-simulator translation can fail silently for some models. NeuroSem would systematise such checks with a protocol battery, tolerances, mutants and held-out evaluation.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (lists given/family names swapped: given 'Lehtimäki', family 'Mikko'); Frontiers event abstract page (WebFetch) gives Mikko Lehtimäki and Marja-Leena Linne, Tampere University of Technology, Neuroinformatics 2014 in Leiden; OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar records match the title and year.
rows.found_via: Crossref bibliographic query (reproducibility neuron model conversion NEURON NeuroML); verified via Crossref works API

rows.citation: Ding J, Zhang D, Hu X-H (2016). An application of metamorphic testing for testing scientific software. Proceedings of the 1st International Workshop on Metamorphic Testing (held with ICSE '16), pp. 37-43. ACM.
rows.model_type: General scientific software (ADDA discrete dipole approximation light-scattering code)
rows.controlled_mutations: unclear - the abstract does not mention mutation analysis; full text not accessed (ACM, closed access).
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - metamorphic relations run related input groups, but these are not neural stimuli.
rows.protocol_optimization: partial - metamorphic relations are refined iteratively during testing; no formal selection or optimization is described.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - an experience report on a single program.
rows.software: none reported in abstract (subject program: ADDA)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Generic prior art on metamorphic testing of scientific code. NeuroSem would use differential reference-vs-transformed comparison with neuroscience protocols, eFEL features, calibrated tolerances and greedy battery selection.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (title, authors, ACM proceedings, pp. 37-43, 2016-05-14, ICSE '16 event); abstract from OpenAlex W2396273285; Semantic Scholar record matches (abstract elided, closed access).
rows.found_via: Crossref bibliographic query (metamorphic testing scientific simulation software); verified via Crossref works API

rows.citation: Kanewala U, Bieman JM, Ben-Hur A (2015). Predicting metamorphic relations for testing scientific software: a machine learning approach using graph kernels. Software Testing, Verification and Reliability 26(3):245-269.
rows.model_type: General scientific software functions (program control-flow/data-dependency graphs)
rows.controlled_mutations: unclear - the abstract does not mention mutation-based assessment; full text not accessed.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - predicts metamorphic relations from program structure, not stimulus sets.
rows.protocol_optimization: partial - machine learning predicts which metamorphic relations apply; no cost-constrained test selection.
rows.heldout_evaluation: unclear - reports prediction accuracy of graph-kernel classifiers; split details not read.
rows.ai_transformations: no - ML is used to build test oracles, not to transform models.
rows.software: none named; the abstract links a dataset of functions at cs.colostate.edu
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Automates finding test oracles for generic code. NeuroSem needs no predicted relations: it compares reference and transformed neuron models on electrophysiology features and learns a compact protocol battery.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (authors, STVR vol 26 issue 3 pp. 245-269, issued 2015-11-16, full abstract); OpenAlex W2280554095 matches. Semantic Scholar lists year 2016, likely the issue year; Crossref's 2015 online date is used.
rows.found_via: Crossref bibliographic query (metamorphic testing scientific simulation software); verified via Crossref works API | Crossref 'metamorphic testing scientific simulation software'; verified via Crossref
